items.body: Ambient label Hibernate have relaunched, returning from a lengthy hiatus – pulling out of their own musical hibernation – well rested, and awakening to a new era despite the steady, soporific state of their new output. Anthéne’s Colour Fields bends and slowly stirs, its head ruffling the pillow and its ambient body grazing the sheets with the first tentative signs of movement after a deep sleep. Its eyes begin to open, and the synths begin to drink in the light. As soon as those lidded shutters are pulled up, the music floats on legs it doesn’t own, levitating in its warm, self-fulfilling light. Colour Fields is a rural form of ambient music, evocative of wide-open plains and swaying oaks drunk on the promises of summer. The music lives in and is a part of an endless field, existing in the fabric of every blade of grass, in a budding lavender bush and a late-to-wake patch of bluebells, oversleeping like a hungover teenager who forgot to set the alarm. The ambient is jettisoned, spreading outwards like a sprinkling of dandelion seeds. The music is as delicate as a wing – one touch, and it would crinkle and crease. In terms of length, Colour Fields is a short release, but it’s perfect as it is, and there should be no time scale when it comes to music. After all, a longer album doesn’t necessarily mean a better album, does it? That train of thought can ruin a musician, who is then forced into lengthening (and subsequently weakening) the album: that kind of obesity and excess is rife in a culture that can’t get enough. Less is always more, and as soon as you start pandering to the thoughts of others, the music ceases to be your own. Hibernate’s new season also includes a new album from Mind Over MIDI. Tussmørke’s quivering, grey-skinned synth reminds one of early science-fiction, while the more pronounced use of electronics adds a good deal of mystery to the music, complete with a dome-shaped flying saucer and all the clichés that accompany such an image. Something has landed in this quiet field, and the cows don’t like it. But the landing isn’t an obvious craft, less an iconic image embedded in popular culture and more like something that stealthily creeps around in the undergrowth. A snaking synth seems to exude a strange form of radiation, capable of incinerating an entire harvest of crops with a mutated form of vitamin D. Water-like melodies run alongside the gentle tweets of birdsong. The melodies themselves seem to hover, lying low over the treescape. Its skin-tearing temperatures quietly and methodically decimate, but the surrounding atmosphere is a stormy sky, a colour close to malignant lead, and as lethal as a speeding bullet. Beats are suppressed, draping low over the background like a metallic curtain. The music’s picked up like a radio wave, but it’s hard to tune out of its frequency once it arrives. You feel it in the pit of your stomach, a steady trickle of indistinct rain or a treble-thin rustling which not only nestles into the mix but invades it, recurring throughout the album along with a skidding synth and the sound of trampling. Those hurried footsteps litter the album – the owner of those worn shoes is running from something, chased through a mile-long cornfield. With its recurring themes and lightless copses, it’s not exactly dark ambient… but it has been exiled. www.hibernate.bandcamp.com
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是厂牌Hibernate结束长期沉寂后的回归之作。Anthéne的《Colour Fields》以田园意象为底色，合成器音色温润而透明，缓慢铺陈出旷野与植物的氛围感——薰衣草丛、风铃草田、蒲公英种子飘散，全都被编织进无垠的声场之中。乐评强调其极简结构与精炼长度，认为'少即是多'的美学远胜于膨胀冗长。Mind Over MIDI的《Tussmørke》则转向冷色调，合成器颤抖如灰色皮肤，电子音色营造出早期科幻式的神秘感与潜在辐射。鸟啼与水流声融入其中，节拍低伏如金属帘幕，整体氛围接近铅灰色风暴天空。两张作品均立足于环境音乐与电子的交叉地带，前者偏自然，后者偏科幻与暗色质地，独立厂牌发行，文字描写充满文学性的感官意象。

items.body:
After the OĽUN album I reviewed enthusiastically a while back, here’s the next project, again motivated and led by violinist/fiddler/composer Ján Kružliak Jr., continuing the rapprochement, indeed embrace, between Slovakia’s traditional music and its classical music. This time it reconnects the works of classical composers who were inspired by and drew on village musics with those traditional sources and styles.
Three ensembles are involved: the Spectrum Quartett led by Kru�liak with two violins, viola and cello; Nogaband, the traditional-style quartet of fiddles, contra (chording viola) and bass that’s led by fiddler and singer Michal Noga; and the female vocal group Ulijanky, plus guest singer Simona Hulejov�.
The majority of the tracks are interpretations of works by Slovak composer Eugen Suchon (1908-1993), with others from fellow-Slovaks Ilja Zeljenka (1932-2007) and Alexander Moyzes (1906-1984), and Hungarian B�la Bart�k (1881-1945) who did a lot of his very detailed collecting of folk music in Slovakia.
In each case the sources - musicians and locations in villages across Slovakia - are credited in the notes, and these arrangements and performances reconnect with the energy and traditional vocal sound of those sources.
In no way is this an orchestra-smoothed thing; this is gutsy, brilliantly played and sung music with all the spirit, skill and technique of traditional music, from players and singers who deeply understand and inhabit it. It’s a glorious piece of work, music to luxuriate in. There’s too much richness to begin to detail, but here’s a dip into a few moments to give the flavor. The tracks all have very long titles detailing their sources, so for brevity’s sake I’ll just give track numbers.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由斯洛伐克小提琴家Ján Kružliak Jr.主导，连接该国传统民间音乐与古典音乐传统。三组音乐家——Spectrum Quartett弦乐四重奏、传统民间风格的Nogaband以及女声组合Ulijanky——共同重新诠释了斯洛伐克作曲家Eugen Suchoň、Ilja Zeljenka、Alexander Moyzes以及匈牙利作曲家巴托克的作品，将这些受民间音乐启发的古典创作与其原始乡村音乐素材进行对照编排。专辑最大的特点在于每一首作品的源头——村庄中的乐人与地点——都在注释中被明确标注。演奏充满原始生命力与传统声乐质感，拒绝古典乐团的精致打磨，展现了对民间传统深刻理解后的鲜活呈现。

items.body: "There is no such thing as a stranger�s children." - old Ukrainian saying I�ve long been affected, indeed somewhat obsessed, by what�s happening in Ukraine, partly because of one of my favorite bands, DakhaBrakha. I went to Kyiv to see them at the time of the Maidan protests, just after the shooting by snipers of over a hundred protesters. I intentionally didn�t read this album�s booklet notes before listening, so that I could react to it without sympathetic pre-judgement, just as music. It�s strong musically and vocally by any standards, Ukrainian or otherwise. When I did then turn to the notes that translate and explain the songs, I had that rare experience, for me, of becoming moist-eyed. The songs are a mix of traditional and original. They are focused on the abduction by Russia of about 20,000 Ukrainian children who have been taken from their parents in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine and sent to Russia, in an attempt to turn them into haters of their native land and people. It�s a heinous war crime. Marichka is a Ukrainian-Canadian singer who moves between Canada and her homeland. For this album she�s gathered two groups of musicians, one in each country. Both ensembles contribute vocals and instrumentation, mostly bowed strings, plus some bandura and piano. The group in Ukraine includes Lisa from the destroyed and invaded city of Mariupol, playing a solo on double ocarina; at 16 she was one of the stolen children but managed to return to Ukraine. Daughters of Donbas � co-led by Marichka and singer/bandurist Alina Kuzma, who shares the lead vocal role � is an all-female ensemble in Canada that tours performing these songs. �Foreign Land� is a reworking of a traditional song about the young girls who were sent away to work in foreign households - Marichka�s grandmother was one of these - that can also be taken to refer to the plight of today�s stolen children. The translation goes: A mother packed up her daughter To leave for a strange land To a strange land with strange people Oh, who will pity you, my daughter? Those who will beat me will pity me I'll never again live with you, my mother When, my daughter, should I expect you to come home? When the grass in the garden grows, my mother The grass grew and grew and began to dry The mother was waiting for her daughter to return, and began to cry Did you hear, my mother, how I came to you? How I flew as a bird above your window? How I cooed like a dove? If, my daughter, I could hear you I would open all the doors and windows To let you fly in Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Alina Kuzma, Zo� Santo As befits the song, Marichka�s vocal here is gentle. But in the second track, �Rusalka,� with Alina Kuzma taking the lead vocals, things turn harsh and fierce. A rusalka is a mythical creature, a nature spirit of fields, forest and rivers, that features in traditional ritual songs. The melody of this one is by Zo� Santo and Kuzma, with lyrics drawing on tradition and the composition of Santo and 19thC Ukrainian poet and folklorist Taras Shevchenko. An ominous double-bass drone, chunking strings, a slithering vocal that moves into sections of white-voice fast recitative and expands into a soaring wild cry. The lyrics are very dark, perhaps evoking the hell of the front line: Home a hell of old growth stumps Marsh a mud of memories Don�t get bogged down in these parts Your kind won�t last a day in here While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. A rusalka sat on a white birch, rusalky asked girls for shirts. Long fingers and nails so sharp Tongue forked round serrated teeth Moss grows down beneath her parts Weeds braided from ear to ear While witches still fly, while roosters have yet to crow, Come here, something arises, �neath the oak something walks. �Girls, my friends, give me your shirts. Though I�m thin, give me a thin one.� Here live us the backless ones Many voices of dead sons You are right to quake in fear Send your sinful children here �Who Am I� is a plea of separation and disorientation, the pain and confusion of an abducted child, contrasting �the human in me� and �the creature in me,� like an internalized riddle-song, with the refrain, in English: Who am I for you? Who am I for me? Do you know me? Really know me? �Enchantress,� passionately sung by Kuzma to her own bandura accompaniment, a girl�s lament of the loss of her brave love taken from her by the enchantress, who is an allegory of war, is based on a traditional song and uses that style of melody and lyrics, �Riddle,� sung by Marichka, reworks a traditional riddle song to be the riddles told by the grandfather of a child, 12-year-old Kira from Mariupol, who experienced the death of her father and her abduction to Russia. Her grandfather tracked her down, and brought her back, traumatized, and asked her riddles - as the notes say �to jog her memory, and remind her who she was, where her home was, and of her family�s love for her.� Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �4.5.0� is a military expression for �all�s well� or �all is quiet.� The song is a message, as from a mother, to a stolen child. Marichka�s voice is cherishing: Remember this: I am with you, I am here Don't give up, I'm with you. Don't give up, I'm with you Your hope is my weapon Don't be sad, I'm with you 4.5.0. will be again �breaking into a tearing howl: And when the world's axis breaks When the sky folds like a parchment Out of nowhere her words will come� �and back to fragile reassurance �It's all right, I'm here, I'm here� "Lullaby," based on a traditional lullaby, sung by Alina Kuzma to accompaniment by her bandura and Zo� Santo's viola, starts in gentle lullaby style, but moves to a lament; it's for the stolen children and those who, as the notes put it, 'have been stolen for ever.' Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, Marichka �Remember, I Believe in You� is a powerful piece of harmonizing vocals and slithering strings. Here�s the story it�s based on: Yevhen lived in Mariupol with his three young children. During the siege they lived in a basement bomb shelter for months. One day, Russian soldiers entered their bomb shelter. Yevhen was taken to a filtration camp and separated from his children who were all taken to a hospital and then to Russian summer �camp�. In the filtration camp Yevhen was brutally tortured and forced to sleep standing on one leg. He tried to fall asleep, whispering prayers for his children: �Everything will be fine, I believe in you.� After his release he walked 30 kilometers to the place where his children had been taken but it was too late. They had already been sent to Moscow. Yevhen learned of this after receiving a text from one of his children who had found an unattended device. He traveled thousands of kilometers, crossed the borders of three countries, endured checks, interrogations and danger to reach Moscow and take his children home. All those days he tirelessly repeated to himself, �I believe in myself, I believe in my kids. Everything will be good.� �Another Heaven,� sung by Marichka with the ensemble in Ukraine, is inspired by another heart-rending story: Ilya was 9 years old when his mother was killed by a rocket strike right in front of him. He was taken to a hospital in occupied Donetsk, where 15 pieces of shrapnel were removed from his body without anesthesia. After he appeared in a report on Russian television, Ilya�s grandmother learned his location. She managed to bring her grandson to Kyiv, where he lives now, experiencing missile attacks every night. At age 11, he says that it is up to everyone to fight enemies, to protect other cities, and to build another heaven, where your home will not be destroyed. In 2014, during the Kyiv Maidan protests, Marichka wrote and performed �Red Boots Tango,� using a melody she�d put to a poem by Taras Shevchenko. For this album she sings it again in Ukraine, with the ensemble there adding swirling, classic tango-style strings. Songs of Stolen Children by Daughters of Donbas, BanduraGirl The final track on the album is a solo, recorded in Kyiv, by Anastasiya Voytyuk, accompanying herself on the older, simpler form of bandura that was used by kobzars to accompany epic poetry, and also on the nowadays more well-known big, heavy form developed from it in Soviet times that was made mainly in the piano factory at Chernihiv. Her song, �Soon I Will Be Back,� is based on a poem by novelist, journalist and war crime researcher Victoria Amelia, who was killed in 2023, in the city of Kramatorsk in Donbas, by a Russian rocket. Find the artist online. Further reading: Otava Yo - Do You Love (Review) Sofia Rei - Umbral (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由乌克兰裔加拿大歌手Marichka与全女性加拿大乐团Daughters of Donbas合作完成，曲目围绕俄罗斯将被占领区约两万乌克兰儿童强制带往本国这一战争罪行展开，以传统乌克兰民歌为基础融合原创作品。编曲以弦乐、班杜拉琴与钢琴为核心，马里乌波尔幸存者Lisa在乌克兰以双陶埙吹奏独奏段落，加拿大与乌克兰两组音乐人共同参与人声与器乐录制。歌曲在温柔与暴烈之间交替，以鲁萨尔卡等斯拉夫民间意象承载对流离失所的哀悼。乐评人前往基辅现场见证革命广场事件后表示，音乐本身的水准与情感冲击力均达到很高标准，专辑在保留传统根基的同时以女性视角重构民族叙事，兼具音乐品质与社会议题力度。

items.body: A confession to begin: I�ve been a fan of Alison Cotton�s music for quite a while, so the announcement of a new album definitely brought me a frisson of delight. The Gods Laugh certainly doesn�t disappoint, with the same deliciously amorphous feel that�s defined her other work, drawing on folk, the avant-garde, as well as a sense of religiosity to make the music here, possibly best exemplified in �I Am!�, where she set a poem by John Clare, England�s great nature poet, to a transcendent melody over the constant underpinning of a lulling drone. While the playing revolves around her usual arsenal of viola, harmonium, hammered dulcimer, and piano, along with some percussion, on this album she also adds some drums, bass and synthesizer. The music is often improvised and captured in a single take, with an almost mystical, hushed sensibility that seems to reach through time, as with �I Still Know You are Calling My Name,� where the tune could have been plucked from an old folk song. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The centerpiece, however, is �Sprigs of Heather,� with an opening that recalls medieval sacred music that becomes a simple, slowly cascading, piano-led melody. It�s far from the longest track on the album, but a little pearl of perfection that carries the listener away. Sprigs of Heather by Alison Cotton The Gods Laugh is a memorial of sorts to Cotton�s father, who died in late 2024. There�s a sense of loss reaching across these tracks, most specifically present on �The Final Harvest,� a solemn piece about her father�s last visit to the allotment he loved so much. It�s suffused with tenderness that extends beyond words. Light and darkness bleed into each other across the music, and moods shift. It�s music that happily stands beyond category, with hints of so many things, but ultimately standing as Alison Cotton music, which might well be all the definition it needs. It will challenge you but also satisfy and move you. What more can you wish from music? Find the artist online. items.body: Those of us who have been digging into Analog Africa�s increasingly formidable releases over the last two decades are well aware of the massive amount of raw, vodun-based Sato and Sakpata-derived funk the label has issued by Benin�s most prolific 1970s-era band, the Orchestre Poly-Ritmo. AA has dropped no fewer than 3 compilations of their heaviest material, as well as a reissue of the band�s first LP, in an effort to give them the international status they deserve. That being said, what might be different about this collection of their music? And who is Antoine Dougb�? Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa As it turns out, Dougb� was a song-conjurer whose mode of musical transfer was slapping his legs in a rhythm known as Cavacha, a groove created by drummer Belobi Meridjo, who was inspired by a train cadence that he worked into a pattern that ultimately spread like a 21st century California wildfire throughout Congolese pop music in the mid-1970s. Dougb�, known as the �Devil�s Prime Minister,� was also a practitioner of vodun who inspired fear in any musician he felt was unsuited to play his music, which is how he landed on working exclusively Poly-Ritmo, as he felt they could nail what he wanted in ways other bands couldn�t. His recording career was brief - 3 albums and a few singles - but as this collection shows, it was potent. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa Because of the era from which this music dates, it�s not surprising that the recording and instrument tones have changed - the guitars have a plastic sheen and synthesizers appear- even if the music remains rooted in the 1970s. Perhaps the influence of the Cuban son is more apparent here than on other Poly-Ritmo collections, especially in the collection�s initial offerings. And yes, Congolese rumba, then shaking all of sub-Saharan Africa to its knees, is present too. �Ma Won Min Towe Leo� is one example. Opening with a bed of synthesizers, the shimmering guitars, tinny, seemingly squeezed dry by the 80s themselves, lock in over relentless high-hat-focused grooves. The guitars finally start firing in different directions midway through, before that synth weaves back in, forming a bed underneath it all. Antoine Dougb� et L'Orchestre Poly-Rythmo De Cotonou 1977 - 1982 (Analog Africa No.44) by Analog Africa �We Tayi Sin Assi Tche� is much more overtly Cuban. With its insistent cowbell, classic, nasal vocal call and response, and tight, repeated guitar figures, its debt to mid-twentieth century Afro-Cuban sons is transparent. Another track, �Djomido Ma Dougbe Tche� rides a groove reminiscent of 70�s-era Franco classic �Liberte.� The pulse is relentless, and the guitar solo repeats a tight repetition of a few notes, driving listeners to ecstasy all the while. However, none of this music is a mere copy of its influences; rather, like so much potent pop coming from the continent at the time, it is a swirl of major influences rendered by local rhythms and vocal phrasing to give it specific identity, in this case, to Benin. Dougb�s musical role on this collection is a bit murky. One of his three albums has a photo of him, fully mic�d behind a collection of hand drums, so perhaps he served as a percussionist/vocalist; this release never explains. He wasn�t a songwriter in the traditional sense. It seems he was more of an instigator and arranger, but his thumbprint was apparently heavy enough to warrant his name on the records he was involved with. Whatever the case, in his brief run as a recording artist, he and Poly-Ritmo produced a handful of driving, Cavacha-inspired grooves that can still wear holes in club floors. Further reading: Petrona Mart�nez - Ancestras (Review) Gnonnas Pedro & His Dadjes - Roi De L'Agbadja Moderne 1974-1983 (Review)

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评聚焦贝宁传奇乐队Orchestre Poly-Rythmo与创作人Antoine Dougbé的合作合集。Dougbé以独特的击腿节奏Cavacha闻名，这一节奏源于鼓手Belobi Meridjo对火车节奏的提炼，后风靡1970年代中期的刚果流行乐界。作为伏都教信仰者，Dougbé对合作乐队极为挑剔，最终只与Poly-Rythmo长期合作。其短暂却浓烈的录音生涯留下三张专辑与若干单曲。音乐层面，由于录制年代跨越七八十年代，乐器音色发生转变——吉他带塑料光泽、合成器加入——但根基仍植于七十年代。评论指出古巴són元素在本作中比Poly-Rythmo其他合集更为明显，辅以刚果rumba影响。文中以《Ma Won Min Towe Leo》为例，解析合成器铺垫、闪闪发光的吉他如何在高帽驱动的律动上交缠。

items.body: Tako Toki are like desert island musicians who, castaway without their instruments, were forced to construct their own. Lucky for us, they are as skilled in making instruments as they are in creating original songs with which to show off their handicrafts. Un Dimanche � Monaco is the band�s follow-up to their well-received debut, Hirsute Farfelus , with a similar mash of musical styles. Before discussing the music, we need to talk about their instrument closet. They really have built everything they play out of bric-a-brac, odds and ends, and rubbish. I�m not sure from listening which is which, but they call their instruments, in an incomplete list, tassofons, tilofons, and tubofones, clarinuts, didjerimou, and klarbass, and my favorite, kitchenofon. (I will refer to what I hear by the names of store-bought instruments that they sound like.) The most surprising thing for me was how accurate the instruments were to pitch and how good they sounded under the harsh scrutiny of modern recording microphones that have documented a rich, high-quality sound. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki They have also very effectively matched their choice of instruments with the style of music that inspires their compositions. Right off the top, �Yinitza� features a laughing clarinet singing a klezmer tune accompanied by bassoon for the bass, frantic two-time percussion, and the exuberant human yelps found on many klezmer recordings. As on this track, many tunes feature improvisations that show an impressive degree of musicianship. On the cumbia-inspired �Le Cuenta,� the characteristic flute carries the tune, augmented by a Spanish singing chorus, and remarkably rich-sounding Latin percussion. The title track surrounds us with afrobeat woodblocks, shakers, and rattles scattered around the mix. The melody is played on a marimba ornamented with bells and cymbals. Again, the lead player improvises over the tune and often against the beat with jazzy chops. The flute returns on the samba-inspired �Ambiguidade,� and on �Aksum� it traces a trance-like Middle Eastern tune reminiscent of a 60s TV spy-show theme. UN DIMANCHE A MONACO - LP by Tako Toki Full of fun and one of a kind, Un Dimanche � Monaco celebrates our universal love of rhythmic, melodic, and harmonic sounds and the varied, wonderful ways cultures have organized that love in what we call music. At the same time, playing on literal pieces of junk, Tako Tiko reminds us, as we contemplate many mall music shops filled with gleaming wood and brass instruments and countless unused guitars lying in closets, that musicians will always find a way to make music. Find the artist online. Further reading: Tako Toki - Hirsute Farfelus (Review) Terje Isungset - Glacial Poetry (Review)

items._cn_summary: Tako Toki乐队以废弃物和零碎物品亲手制作乐器，包括tassofon、kitchenofon等自创名称的乐器，在现代录音技术的严格审视下仍展现出准确的音高和丰富的音质。专辑融合多元世界音乐风格：克莱兹默曲调配合笑声单簧管和巴松管，库姆比亚启发下运用西班牙合唱与拉丁打击乐，非洲节拍轨道铺陈木鱼与沙锤，桑巴风格由横笛主导，另有一条中东旋律线贯穿。乐评特别赞赏乐队对乐器选择与风格定位的把控能力，以及乐手在即兴段落中展现的扎实技巧。专辑传递出一种普世的音乐理念：音乐家总能找到发声的方式，无论手边拥有的是精雕细琢的乐器还是废品。这张作品延续了前作的风格基础上进一步探索自制乐器的可能性，是独立厂牌下具有实验精神的创作。

items.body: After the extra-terrestial explorations of Eventyrferd , the previous album from Norway's Camilla Hole Trio, in which sci-fi synth sounds were married with traditional material, their latest release Langs is rather more earthbound. But the quest to look beyond their own country's folk music continues. Camilla Hole's main instrument being the soprano sax, the influence of jazz is unsurprising and this is evident in the opening track �Springleik,� signifying a tune used to accompany the springleik dance from the west of Norway. Initially Hole takes the melody with Egil Kalman and Knut Kvifte Nesheim providing rhythmic support on double bass and drums respectively, with the overdubbing of Kalman's modular synth and Nesheim's vibraphone adding colour. But characteristically for this trio, in which assigned roles are never clearly defined or adhered to, things soon start to move around, with Kalman taking up the melody on his bass, playing the melody in unison with Hole, while Nesheim opens things out further rhythmically. As the whole piece takes on a much more improvisatory feel, Hole plays the melody one more time as things draw to a close. Langs by Camilla Hole Trio

items._cn_summary: Camilla Hole Trio 的新专辑延续了上一张将科幻合成器音色与传统挪威民谣融合的思路，但整体风格回归更为质朴的地面感。高音萨克斯手 Camilla Hole 与贝斯手 Egil Kalman、鼓手 Knut Kvifte Nesheim 三人之间的角色分配刻意模糊，开篇曲目"Springleik"以西挪威传统舞曲旋律为基础，起初由 Hole 主奏旋律，Kalman 与 Nesheim 以贝斯和鼓提供节奏支撑，随后叠加 Kalman 的模块合成器与 Nesheim 的颤音琴丰富音色层次。乐评特别指出，作品发展过程中三人不断交换角色——Kalman 转而用贝斯与 Hole 齐奏旋律，Nesheim 拓展节奏维度——整首曲目逐渐转向即兴化展开，最终由 Hole 再次收束旋律。这一动态的角色流动与即兴结构是这支三重奏的标志性特征，体现出对挪威民谣素材的开放性再诠释。

items.body: Kr�ta , the latest release on Norway's Taragot label, features a Swede and two Norwegians playing interpretations of mainly traditional tunes from their respective countries. Fiddler Mats Ed�n has long been involved in Swedish folk music, as a player, composer and teacher, and in the process exploring and integrating different musical styles and approaches. Tellef Kvifte was in the pioneering Norwegian crossover band Slinkombas in the 1970s and has continued to play a central role in Norwegian folk music, both as a musician and an academic. Most often heard playing the sj�fl�yte , more widely known as a recorder, Kvifte has employed other instruments from outside the Norwegian tradition, in particular the saxophone and bagpipes. His son Knut Kvifte Nesheim , a drummer and composer, has also shown a determination to blur the lines between different musical genres, both in his solo and group projects. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio It comes as no surprise then to find this trio offering a far from conventional take on the tunes they have chosen. While dance tunes may be the source of most of the material here, this feels more akin to chamber music; not that it is remotely classical in style, but in the sense it conveys of three players engrossed in a musically intimate conversation. This is not a performance appropriate for accompanying dancers but might instead be seen as an exploration of hidden possibilities of meaning in the music. In so doing it reveals some of its underlying mystery, including, perhaps, a darker side. Just as in an Ibsen play, where the surface bonhomie, jollity and social nicety can be hiding something more sinister, in Scandinavian dance music there are at times hints of a troublesome undercurrent below the surface. So the decision to open proceedings with �Fossgrimen,� a fiddle tune from Norway's Setesdal valley, is perhaps significant. A fossgrimen is a mythical creature, a kind of water-sprite living in waterfalls from whom fiddle-players were considered to have learned their skills and for that were not universally welcomed, with the fiddle considered to be the devil's instrument. Kr�ta by Ed�n/Kvifte/Nesheim trio Tellef Kvifte takes the lead melody on most tracks but on the Swedish �Polska from Per Myhr,� having played a repeated introductory riff on the sj�fl�yte, with Mats Ed�n providing an amorphous textural accompaniment below and Nesheim adding some quiet tinkling, it's Ed�n who introduces the tune on the fiddle with Kvifte proceeding to play in unison. It's a short track and almost as soon as it gets going things start to fragment and everything grind to a halt.

items._cn_summary: 这是一张由瑞典小提琴手与两位挪威乐手组成的三重奏专辑，以室内乐式的亲密对话重新诠释斯堪的纳维亚传统舞曲素材。乐评指出，虽然素材多源自挪威和瑞典的民间舞曲，但演奏方式远离舞蹈伴奏功能，更接近三位演奏家沉浸于音乐内部对话的探索。他们刻意挖掘舞曲表面欢愉之下的暗流与神秘感，以挪威Setesdal山谷的小提琴曲《Fossgrimen》开场，呼应民间传说中水妖传授琴艺的意象。编曲中，竖笛、小提琴与打击乐形成层次分明的纹理，旋律片段在展开后迅速碎裂瓦解，展现出对传统素材的解构意图。专辑呈现出学院派气质与实验性并存的特质，将北欧民间传统置于当代室内即兴的框架中审视。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / sound documentary / free verse
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑并非传统音乐作品，而是录音师Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区暴力街区采集的声音文献。二十五位枪支暴力幸存者在前廊就地讲述自身经历，参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等。录音没有任何添加音乐，仅保留环境底噪与说话者的呼吸声，形成原始的田野录音加口述自白结构。项目在特朗普下令部署国民警卫队同一天进行，地点临近中途机场航道下方的社区。专辑收益捐赠给Cure Violence Global。编辑选择以录音师本人简短评论加原始声轨呈现，放弃传统乐评框架，强调让社区自己的声音说话。艺术价值在于将日常悲剧转化为听觉证词，旁观者与亲历者边界模糊，形成一种介于声音艺术与社会档案之间的特殊文本。

items._cn_summary: 这是休斯顿Lawndale艺术与表演中心的一场实验音乐演出，由Nameless Sound主办。演出包含两组音乐家的即兴合作：Gabriel Martinez（打击乐）、Dan Miñoza（吉他）与Leif Steenson（合成器）组成的三重奏，加上Anthony Almendárez（小号、电子）和Amaru.Nomad（行进上低音号、粗管短号、采样器）组成的双人组合。这种编制融合了原声乐器、电子设备和采样技术，体现出自由即兴和实验音乐场景中常见的跨媒介探索。演出内容涉及噪音、实验声响和自由演奏的多个领域，体现了休斯顿本地地下实验音乐圈的活力。需要指出的是，由于原文为演出信息介绍而非深度乐评，关于实际音乐质量和艺术水准的评价信息有限，因此评分保持适中。

items.body: Gilla Band Pugnello Dublin rock band deliver their most punishing record to date Pugnello by Gilla Band Have you ever heard a song for the first time and felt a shiver run so deep it took the floor with it? That, for me, is the first seconds of Pugnello, and it hardly relents from there. Dara Kiely comes in screaming on ‘The Angelus’, all scalded shriek, hollering about Bananas in Pyjamas and Gary Lineker as crisp maniac. The track pitches somewhere between Lightning Bolt and a ten-thousand-mile thundercloud, Adam Faulkner’s rolls hurtling underneath like Swans at triple speed. The title rewires the Angelus, RTÉ’s evening bell, into a street preacher bawling in tongues. That opener alone would underline everything they’ve been since France 98... items._cn_summary: 爱尔兰都柏林乐队Gilla Band在《Pugnello》中呈现出迄今最具攻击性的作品。开场曲《The Angelus》以Dara Kiely尖锐嘶吼开篇，歌词将英国儿童电视节目与足球明星拼贴为癫狂意象，鼓击与吉他滚奏在高速驱动下交织出暴烈张力。专辑标题本身即是一次解构实验——将爱尔兰国家广播公司的晚祷钟声改写为街头传教士的狂乱讲道，赋予日常声音以异化含义。整体创作延续乐队自《France》以来的脉络，在后朋克与噪音摇滚传统中注入噪音实验与文本断裂手法。The Quietus的短评虽篇幅有限，但精准捕捉了专辑从首秒起即建立的持续压迫感与文化挪用策略。

items.body: “Curandera” opens Bestiaria with a healer giving instructions. “Niña / Escucha cómo tu cuerpo te habla,” sings Ana Karen G. Barajas of Karen y Los Remedios: girl, listen to how your body talks to you. The song comes from Karen’s own illness and from the women in her family who saw her through it with advice, recipes and limpias, the cleansing rituals Mexican grandmothers pass down. The curandera in the lyric hands the work back to the girl, telling her to listen to her body and to how her soul breathes, and warns her that “Cuando callas te guardas / Lo malo / Y lo bueno”: stay silent and you keep the bad in with the good. Karen, guitarist Guillermo Berbeyer and Mexico City producer Jiony set it as a dark cumbia over a low bass and a steady beat. Trombone and cowbell sit around her voice, an organ hangs at the back of the mix, and in the instrumental breaks synth and guitar lines take over. She lives in Hong Kong now, a long way from the Mexico City she was born in and the Guanajuato she grew up in. Bestiaria, the follow-up to 2023’s Silencio, builds its twelve songs around twelve figures, among them the agave goddess Mayahuel and the Fates of “Las Moiras”. “Curandera” is the fourth single from it. items._cn_summary: 《Curandera》作为Karen y los Remedios专辑《Bestiaria》的第四支单曲，以墨西哥传统治疗仪式为创作根基，将女性家族代际传承的清洁仪式与身体疗愈经验转化为歌词文本。音乐上由墨西哥城制作人Jiony操刀，在低沉贝斯与稳定节拍之上构建暗色调cumbia框架，长号与牛铃环绕人声，合成器与吉他线条在器乐间奏中交替推进，背景悬挂的管风琴音色增添仪式氛围。整张专辑围绕十二个形象展开，从龙舌兰女神Mayahuel到命运女神Las Moiras，延续2023年《Silencio》的神话叙事路线。艺术家本人现居香港，与墨西哥城出生、瓜纳华托成长的背景形成跨地域文化张力，为作品注入离散视角。整体呈现拉丁世界音乐与电子制作融合的方向。

items.body: My sins are all forgiven. I might be desperate, but I won’t let you forget. I know you will give in to me. I am dead set. I am dead set. She 1 • Him 2 have built their latest single Obsessed around one of pop music’s most reliable bad ideas: somebody confusing romantic destiny with a complete inability to take no for an answer. The Cleveland duo of Evan Nave and Cassie Bishop bring years of Lestat and Shy Moon behind them, though Obsessed feels leaner and brighter than that résumé might suggest. The synths skip forward in sharp little patterns, Bishop keeps her vocal airy and cool, and underneath it all sits an electroclash streak that brings to mind the clipped attitude and wiry pop economy of Elastica fed through a rack of 80s electronics. There is plenty of Human League, Yazoo, Soft Cell, and Ladytron in the bloodstream, but the guitars give the track an extra shove. Producer Michael Seifert threads in parts with a distinctly Fixx-like character, adding just enough bite to keep the arrangement from becoming too polished for its own good. “This song has been amazing to put together,” says Nave. “An 80s vibe with a very modern spin. And our producer, Michael Seifert, dropped some very Fixx-like guitars on it. Love the dark lyrical tone versus the upbeat music dichotomy.” That contrast is where Obsessed starts getting funny in a slightly alarming way. The music suggests somebody having a marvelous time under bright club lights; the lyrics suggest that somebody has already memorized your commute. Bishop drew inspiration from the horror film Obsession and its character Nikki, played by Inde Navarrette. “I wrote the lyrics to this song based off the movie Obsession, which I loved and thought was a unique and fun idea for a horror movie,” says Bishop. “I wanted to capture some of the elements and mood of the film in this piece.” She certainly found the right emotional neighborhood. The character at the center of the song barrels through pleading, certainty, possession, and total romantic entitlement while treating every objection as a temporary inconvenience. Love becomes less a mutual arrangement than a hostile takeover conducted in excellent makeup. Bishop wisely keeps her delivery light. She never overplays the menace, and that restraint makes the character more convincing. The voice remains smooth, composed, almost sweet, even as the lyrics tighten their grip. It gives Obsessed the unnerving quality of someone smiling pleasantly while explaining why the two of you are obviously meant to spend eternity together. The electroclash edge helps, too. Those angular guitars and bright electronics give the song a brisk, fashionable nastiness, somewhere between synthpop precision and the kind of deadpan cool Elastica once made look effortless. Obsessed is catchy enough to dance to and unhinged enough to make you reconsider sharing your location. Romance, apparently, remains a dangerous hobby. The charming video channels that same bubbly sycophancy inside the studio, where eager autograph and selfie seekers chase the performers around, hoping for — and eventually fighting over — a moment with their idols. There is something wonderfully silly about the escalation, and visually it brings to mind Toni Basil’s Mickey, with its bright, performative enthusiasm and choreographed fan frenzy. The joke fits the song neatly: admiration is only one bad decision away from fixation. Watch the video for Obsessed below: Listen to Obsessed below and order the single here. items._cn_summary: 克利夫兰二人组She 1 • Him 2的单曲《Obsessed》以明亮跳跃的合成器节奏与尖锐的电吉他线条构建出一首带有八十年代新浪潮血统的合成流行作品。歌词取材于恐怖电影中关于执念与浪漫占有欲的主题，主唱Bishop以冷静轻盈的声线呈现出表面柔和、内心偏执的反差感，旋律与阴暗文本之间产生一种微妙的喜剧张力。制作人Michael Seifert为编曲加入了具有Fixx风格的吉他质感，使得整体音色在合成器的精致之外保留了适度的粗粝边缘。作品融汇了Human League、Yazoo、Soft Cell、Ladytron以及Elastica的影响，在合成流行框架内注入暗潮与后朋克的棱角，形成既适合俱乐部舞池又令人不安的听感。

items.body: The Future arrived Tuesday No one knew, however A girl packing her suitcase saying, “Maybe now or never” There is a bassline in Ganser’s Futuretripping that seems to know the economy is fake, the clocks are lying, and somebody somewhere is trying to sell you another subscription to tomorrow. Around it, Brian Cundiff’s guitars jab and veer while Alicia Gaines sings with the cool composure of someone watching the machinery malfunction exactly as expected. The result lands somewhere between Bikini Kill, The Breeders, and DEVO, all wired together by a song obsessed with time, delay, and the peculiar modern habit of waiting for permission to panic. Futuretripping is a wiry, nervy post-punk offering built from elastic bass, restless guitar, and the kind of lyrical absurdity that makes modern life sound only slightly more ridiculous than it already is. Somewhere between The Breeders, Bikini Kill, and DEVO, the song turns anxiety about time, media, and collective hesitation into something sharp enough to dance to. The track picks up the rhythmic intelligence that ran through Animal Hospital, the band’s third LP, while pushing the tension into a tighter frame. The bassline keeps the song in motion with a thick, spring-loaded bounce, while the guitar scratches and darts around it with nervous energy. Alicia Gaines sings with a dry, controlled delivery that gives the song’s stranger images room to land without forcing the joke. The lyrics revolve around a world trapped in endless anticipation. Screens insist that everything is going according to plan, people wait for the next signal, and tomorrow becomes something they can apparently borrow from a shady acquaintance with the right connections. Ganser turns that uncertainty into deadpan comedy, presenting the future as another dubious commodity sold to people who have already spent too much of the present waiting around. The image of someone selling umbrellas beneath a clear sky gets at the song’s humor perfectly. It is ridiculous, vaguely ominous, and just believable enough. “Ahead of going on the road with Bikini Kill, I was interested in the concept of cheating time, where one could go for just a little more of it,” says Gaines. “After coming back from Europe earlier this year, we found our personal senses of time were distorted as we were dropped back into life in Chicago, mixing the mundane with the fantastical. Reaching into tomorrow for a little more of today became an inside joke, now Futuretripping.” Cundiff frames that temporal confusion as something closer to collective agitation. “Everybody’s waiting for the sign to change,” he says. “People tend to wait around to be fed what they should react to these days, what to do, and I suppose there’s a bit of that restlessness in the music and lyrics as well. It’s an agitation that it’s not tomorrow while also wanting more time today, right now.” Gaines also directs the accompanying video, which leans into a loose ’90s montage aesthetic, cutting random footage against the band performing beneath a bright blue sky. The editing has the same sideways humor as the song, constantly shifting between ordinary images and mildly surreal interruptions. Ganser leave us with a world where everybody is waiting for the sign to change while the sign itself appears to have wandered off. Watch the video for Futuretripping below: Chicago’s Ganser have spent the years since their 2018 debut Odd Talk developing an increasingly restless conversation between post-punk, noise rock, and art-school absurdity. Just Look At That Sky followed in 2020, while the 2022 EP Nothing You Do Matters brought Liars’ Angus Andrew into the producer’s chair. Bassist and vocalist Alicia Gaines and drummer Brian Cundiff remain central to the band’s writing, balancing physical rhythms with dry humor and an eye for the contradictions of everyday life. Their third album, Animal Hospital, was released through Felte on August 29, 2025, with production shared by Ganser and Andrew. A deluxe edition followed on April 22, 2026, adding five alternate versions of songs from the record. Touring with IDLES, Mclusky, and Ted Leo has helped sharpen their live attack; this September, Ganser joined Bikini Kill for shows in Milwaukee, Chicago, Royal Oak, and Cleveland. Futuretripping, released September 10, extends that momentum with a new song written and arranged by Gaines and Cundiff. For future live announcements and ticket links, visit Ganser’s official shows page. Listen to Ganser’s Future Tripping below, and order the single here. items._cn_summary: Ganser 来自芝加哥后朋克阵营，新单曲《Futuretripping》以弹性贝斯线为核心骨架，搭配吉他的紧张刮擦与冷峻人声，形成介于 Bikini Kill、The Breeders 与 DEVO 之间的神经质张力。歌词围绕时间错位、屏幕幻象与集体等待展开，将对未来不确定性的焦虑转化为冷面喜剧，配以阳光下卖伞的荒诞意象延续这一主题。编曲上延续了乐队第三张专辑《Animal Hospital》的节奏智慧，但结构更为紧致。视频由主唱 Gaines 亲自执导，进一步强化了歌中虚实交错的视觉叙事。整体延续后朋克传统，未做大幅跨界融合，但在歌词概念与音色处理上展现出独立的艺术自觉。

items.body: Achachay is what highland Ecuadorians say when the cold catches them, arraray when the heat does. Both words came into Andean Spanish from Quichua, and BRITTA builds “Achachay” on the pair: a love song about wanting someone enough to feel both. A requinto line, the small high-tuned guitar of Ecuadorian string music, runs over percussion drawn from the country’s Pacific coast and a trap low end. The alt-pop production leaves the guitar exposed and the beat holds a steady pressure under a vocal that stays at the point of anticipation. Born in Ambato in the central Ecuadorian Andes and based in Los Angeles in the US, Britta has been feeding Ecuadorian traditional forms into dance production for a while: on her single “NON3 (no te dejes avecilla)” she sampled her own voice singing an albazo, the fast triple-time song form of the Ecuadorian highlands, and built a house track around it. “Achachay” points that same working method at Latin alternative, with the Andean Spanish idioms running through the lyric carrying as much of the song’s identity as the requinto and the percussion do. items._genre: Latin alternative / Andean folk / electronic fusion
items._cn_summary: 厄瓜多尔裔洛杉矶制作人BRITTA以"Achachay"（安第斯西班牙语中形容寒冷带来的体感反应）为概念核心，将厄瓜多尔高原的requinto高音吉他、太平洋沿岸打击乐与trap低音融合，形成alt-pop框架下的跨文化电子作品。她的方法论在于提取传统音素的本质特征——高山albazo三拍速节奏、凯楚亚语词汇——然后将其拆解并重新嵌入当代电子舞曲结构中。歌词层面，安第斯西班牙语习语成为音乐身份的重要载体，与器乐配置平分秋色。这种将原声采样自身演唱的folk片段并解构为house节拍的工作方式，体现了一种持续的民族音乐学式的制作思维。该作展现出在拉丁另类场景中融合传统与现代的明确方向感。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — A south Korean group that took 18 years to release their first album and the least one can say isthat Superstring didn't take the easy road. Yes their main influence is classical music, but theywouldn't name have named their kids Ludwig, Johan Sebastian or Wolfgang Amadeus. They might havethought of Edgar, Karlheinz or Gabriel, though. BTW, it's not just about modern classical , as thereare hints of jazz dispersed throughout the duration of their first works. Noteworthy, TGD was firstreleased as vinyl-only, waiting some three years to finally release it in the user-friendly formatcalled CD.Indeed, while relatively dissonant, SS is not extreme Avant Prog like Guapo would be, but they'renot very careful about your sanity beyond your eardrums. Their Grand Design is still relativelyaccessible, if you like atmospheric improvisation, almost cinematic, gloomy ambiances with also PostRock moments. This instrumental quintet will be remarkably stable throughout their career, focusingon the violin and piano as lead instruments, but backed up by a guitar. There are some lovelymoments, but also plenty of tense passages, not necessarily providing a release outlet for thenervous accumulation.TBH, not my cup or tea, but it's definitely worth their Bandcamp detour at least once, even if itwill never be an essential piece of work. Add another half-star, though !!!
items._cn_summary: Superstring 是一支韩国器乐五重奏乐队，经历十八年才推出首张专辑，乐评指出他们的音乐以现代古典为核心，夹杂爵士元素，由小提琴与钢琴担任主奏，辅以吉他，整体氛围偏向阴郁、近似电影配乐般的大气感。虽然作品存在一定不协和与紧张段落，但并非极端前卫，尚在可接受范围内。最初以黑胶形式发行，三年后才推出CD版本。评论者认为专辑并非自己的心头好，但仍值得在Bandcamp上至少试听一次，并给予额外半分加分。这张作品在学院派古典与爵士之间寻找平衡，融合了大气感即兴与后摇滚片段，展现出一种不急不躁但略显沉闷的实验倾向。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — Third album in three years after taking 18 years to create their first one, Architecture might sound/read like a logical successor to their previous one, but there is quite a sonic progression here;eve,n if SS' collective paws are plainly recognizable. Indeed, we've taken a steep turn away from Avant-Prog, but I"m not sure this is due to the new arrival Katie's saxophone on three tracks, because it doesn't really change the overall soundscapes, even if the energy reach a different level and intensity - for the better, I might add. But indeed, the general sonic direction of this album tells us that we are at a corner of the band's career.The dissonance element present in their first two albums has almost disappeared, and this helps the accessibility o�f their music. Relatively absent from their first two album, there is a sense of drama permeating most of the tracks, endearing us to their musical escapes and extravaganzas. Emotional melodies over tight rhythms. BTW, it was their first album directly sold in CD, and for both formats, SS took the carte to make an attractive sleeve with a transparent protecting plastic sleeve. TBH, I really don't know why the band will change its name and record label (I guess the departure of their violinist played a big role), after the release of their best-yet album . But there will be two undeniable links: the Architecture link (purposely misspelled) and the same type of line-up (new violinist) and a now-permanent sax player replacing the too-discreet guitarist. but that's for their next album. In the meantime, their third is definitely the one I preferred at the time.
items._cn_summary: 这是乐队三年内发行的第三张专辑，相较前作在声音方向上有显著转变：不和谐元素大幅减少，旋律的可听性提升，整体情感浓度增强，情绪张力渗透于多数曲目。乐评指出新加入的萨克斯手仅在三首作品中出现，并未从根本上改变乐队的声音质感，但提升了能量的强度与层次。评论强调专辑呈现出乐队生涯转折点的特征：戏剧性叙事取代了早期的不和谐美学，紧凑节奏之上的情感化旋律成为主导。此外，评论还提及乐队可能因小提琴手离队而调整了编制与厂牌，并对专辑实体包装设计给予正面评价。整体来看，这是一张在延续核心辨识度的同时向更易接受方向过渡的转型之作。

items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — Recorded simultaneously with its hostile and murky counterpart, "Deliverance", during the summer of 2002, the gentler and more melancholic "Damnation" - Opeth's seventh album - didn't see the light of day until April 2003, due to their record label's decision to separate the two releases for commercial reasons. An album unexpectedly devoid of Mikael �kerfeldt's guttural vocals, the brutal riffs and abrasive textures that had defined the Swedish band, and their usual monolithic instrumental displays, the result of �kerfeldt's deliberate intention to immerse himself in the smoother, more experimental side of 1970s progressive rock, accompanied for this purpose by the fantastic Steven Wilson, whose decisive work as co-producer and musician brings a sensibility and sonic aesthetic that resonate with those of his band, Porcupine Tree.While it's true that in their earlier work Opeth included acoustic and refreshing sections amid their stormy arrangements, on "Damnation" they take it a step further by devoting its just over forty-three minutes to dreamy melodies set in an introspective and tense atmosphere that flows unhurriedly over the misty, ethereal soundscapes woven by Wilson's Mellotrons and Peter Lindgren's clean, serene guitars. Tracks like the hypnotic "Windowpane," with its magnificent jazz-inspired solo, or the psychedelic "In My Time of Need," "Death Whispered a Lullaby," and "Closure" evoke the most dreamlike and hazy side of genre icons such as King Crimson, the pre-"The Dark Side of the Moon" Pink Floyd, and the Gabriel-era Genesis.And staying true to that evocative, immersive vibe, the instrumental "Ending Credits," with its long guitar bends reminiscent of Camel's Andy Latimer, and the impeccable backing -as throughout the album- from the standout Mart�n M�ndez on bass and Martin Lopez on percussion, along with the trance-like and unchanging "Weakness," featuring a whispering, spectral �kerfeldt, ultimately round out "Damnation": the beginning of Opeth's stylistic transition and one of the most controversial phases of their career.3.5/4 stars

items.body: For an overview of the what, the why, and the where of this music, do read my review of Volume 1 of this series. Essentially, this collection is more of what made Volume 1 so infectious. Yet, what makes this music so fascinating in general, that is, beyond its unswerving ability to fill dance floors, is the fact that these two islands, part of the Paises Africanos de Lingua Oficial Portuguesa (PALOP) regions of the world, are the second smallest African country; Seychelles is smaller. There are only 12 villages on Sao Tom�, lots of rain forest and, not surprisingly, lots of rain. I mention this because one could be fooled into thinking, with music like what�s on offer here, there must have been a music scene larger than there actually was. Not that little was happening, but that less got recorded or released than it might have had there been a city such as Lagos or Nairobi with the studios, labels, and pressing plants to better document it all. The music here, like Volume 1- recorded during Africa�s so-called golden age- is known as Puxa, a complex stew of ingredients from other former African Portuguese colonies mixed with rhythms that, with the help of dancers, can summon spirits or exorcise demons. At least according to some. It�s worth knowing that a 100 years or so ago, the Portuguese banned Puxa dance; it�s also worth knowing they appear to have failed miserably at this silly endeavor. Tucked away in modern Puxa is merengue, Kompas, Soukouss, Benga, and much else. One suspects much of this is coincidental, while other grooves were definitely imported considering both Portuguese rule and the islands� location over the Atlantic from the Caribbean. But don�t be fooled into thinking these two islands don�t have their own thing, as the sounds on this collection show. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s - Pedro Lima Pedro Lima, who has featured in his own Bongo Joe collection, leads a fiery band, complete with choked guitar vamps tussling with a kit drummer as a lead guitar comments from the sidelines on �Sossegado.� Elsewhere, Sangazuza demonstrates what happens when the bass and keys drop out, leaving the drummers and guitars to ride out a groove and drive dancers mad in the process. Check �Sono s� ku� de t�ma� or �Mairo bi cedo� for their ability to place a firm finger on the pulse. Over 15 tracks, the collection shows off multiple guitars weaving and circling one another, with lead and harmony vocals constantly in response, becoming part of the songs� melodic framework. At any given moment, vocals give way as the music unspools and floats on grooves that must have gone on for hours live. Africa Negra�s �Apoi�mos a luta dos nossos irm�os� is one example. L�VE L�VE Vol. 2: Sao Tom� & Principe Sounds 70s-80s by Various Artists In general, what�s on offer here, like Volume 1, was recorded at Radio Sao Tom� e Principe (RSTP), often taped in the courtyard outside at night, and released on cassette or occasionally, vinyl. It captures the joy of post-1975 independence and only fizzled out as styles changed and musicians struggled to make ends meet. Yet, take a quick listen to recent RSTP programming, which features musicians such as Babilonia or Calema, and you�ll still hear Puxa rhythms, showing just how potent the music form this two-island nation is on a global level. And Bongo Joe, who have also released two volumes featuring the above mentioned Africa Negra, have given this music the treatment it deserves, with extensive notes on the country�s history, vintage photographs, and band discographies. items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，由北欧民间乐坛经验丰富的歌手Mia Guldhammer领衔。五首曲目大多取材自传统音乐，乐手各自带来不同视角。开场曲以粗粝奔放的节奏展示了Guldhammer极具说服力的嗓音；唯一原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus创作，口簧琴与风笛提供持续的推进力。钦巴龙琴为传统曲目营造精致底色，Guldhammer的口簧琴与其他乐器交织，簧片与长笛、弦乐在终曲中融合出令人兴奋的失衡感。整体弥漫着古老而略带吱呀的氛囲，展现了乐队早熟而精湛的功力。

items._cn_summary: 本文介绍德国乐队Popol Vuh为赫尔佐格1974年纪录片《木雕师施泰纳的伟大迷狂》所创作的完整配乐即将首次以官方形式发行。此前该配乐仅以乐迷自录的音频流传，此次将发行黑胶与数字版本。专辑还收录了james K、ML Buch和Lorenzo Senni三位艺术家对'施泰纳的迷狂'这首曲目的全新改编。赫尔佐格的影片讲述了瑞士跳台滑雪选手Walter Steiner的故事，他在全职做木匠的同时追逐跳台滑雪的世界纪录，并痴迷于另一项运动。Popol Vuh的配乐以冥想式氛围和东方音乐元素著称，与赫尔佐格的影像美学长期契合。此次官方发行为乐迷提供了接触这部罕见作品的机会，同时也通过当代电子艺术家的再创作，将经典配乐置于当下语境中重新审视。

items.body: Review by brainsuccasurgery — *Limite Acque Sicure* by *Limite Acque Sicure*?a surprising title and surname, a sort of metaphor with multiple possible levels of meaning: the cartographic contours of the Mediterranean Sea in the Middle Ages? A body of water of a certain depth, not to be exceeded? The knowledge of our inner selves (or that of others), beyond which it may be dangerous to venture? The need to push past our own limits in order to grow? Or simply the name of a red wine from Abruzzo? Please refer to the very interesting lyrics on this album for a hint of an answer (be sure to have an Italian translation tool on hand if you don't speak the language). Musically speaking, you don't need to be an expert on Banco's music to understand that *Limite Acque Sicure*, hailing from Ferrara and formed in 2005 by singer Andrea Chendi and keyboardist Antonello Giovannelli as just one of many tribute bands, is a true devotee of the golden age of the Nocenzi brothers' band?a fact confirmed by the inclusion on this self-titled album of the iconic "Il Giardino Del Mago" (Banco 1972), in a dazzling live version.Between the introductory "Sogno D'Oriente" (12:48)?with its oriental sounds, as its name suggests, reminiscent of the famous "Kashmir"?and the short "Ti Salver� " (2:11)?placed at the other end, in the style and spirit of Banco's "Traccia II" (that album again) Certain tracks on *Limite Acque Sicure* stand out more. These are the ones where the band most clearly demonstrates that it has something personal to convey to us. "Terra Straniera" (7:53), with its majestic, enthusiastic, and determined finale, is closer in style to *Prowlers* than to *Banco*; "Il Respiro Dell'Anima" (8:25), with its more lively rhythm, ambitious structure, and shimmering arrangements that leave plenty of room for highly effective guitar and Moog solos. And above all, the epic "Fiamme Intorno " (10:48), with a darker main theme (though carried by a deceptively light rhythm), as if weighed down by a relentless exploration of humanity's spiritual wanderings, then giving way to a second, more open and luminous section, full of hope, whose coda?and this is quite unexpected?features a few drum beats dedicated to? Neil Peart. On a more contemporary note, the music of Limite Acque Sicure evokes memories of Museo Rosenbach, Campo Di Marte, Il Rovescio Della Medaglia, Alphataurus, and Apoteosi, all those meteor-like bands that shone for the duration of a single album (often released in 1973) before disappearing for a long time?or forever. "Limite Acque Sicure" seems to be a tribute to the RPI of the past, yet one that looks toward the future. In other words, it is less a relic of a glorious past than a promise of what the RPI may have in store.

items._cn_summary: 这张来自意大利费拉拉的自命名专辑延续了七十年代意大利前卫摇滚黄金时期的血脉，以键盘为主导的器乐编排向Banco del Mutuo Soccorso致敬。专辑包含翻唱经典曲目《Il Giardino Del Mago》的现场版本，开篇十二分钟的东方主题段落呼应Led Zeppelin的《Kashmir》，终曲则借鉴Banco的《Traccia II》手法。原创作品如《Terra Straniera》、《Il Respiro Dell'Anima》和长达近十一分钟的《Fiamme Intorno》展示了乐队对宏伟结构、Moog合成器独奏与电吉他对话的掌控，后者结尾向Rush鼓手Neil Peart致敬。整张专辑既是回顾，也是对意大利前卫摇滚未来可能性的承诺，但本质上仍是对传奇遗产的致敬之作，而非突破性实验。

items.body: Dark synthwave producer Das Mörtal releases the two-track single “DRAIN ME” on Lisbon Lux Records on 30 September 2026. The single pairs the original version with a remix by synthwave producer Dan Terminus, and precedes Das Mörtal’s mini-album “DECVY I,” out 29 October 2026. Das Mörtal, the project of Montreal-based producer Cristóbal Cortes, describes “DRAIN ME” as “a track about the feeling of running in circles in the health care system while being drained from the multiple tests one person might go through.” The track opens with a cinematic, sweeping tone before shifting into a fast-paced, techno-driven rhythm section with an arpeggiated synth pluck, washed-out vocals and a half-time breakdown before its final chorus. Dan Terminus, grouped alongside Perturbator, Carpenter Brut and GosT as one of what press materials call the “Four Horsemen of Synthwave,” reworks “DRAIN ME” with chopped and manipulated vocals, punchy percussion and an occasional violin line over booming basslines that combine acoustic and synthesised elements. “DRAIN ME” follows the double single “Parasite & Ghost,” which Das Mörtal released on Lisbon Lux Records on 4 June 2026, also ahead of “DECVY I.” An official teaser for “DRAIN ME” is available on YouTube, and the single is available to pre-save via ffm.to/drainmee. About Das Mörtal Das Mörtal is the project of Cristóbal Cortes, an electronic music producer and DJ based in Montreal whose work began in Berlin, drawing on artists including Steve Moore and Aphex Twin. Das Mörtal’s sound blends techno, occult electro and Italo disco into a dark, nostalgic style informed by German techno as well as horror and science-fiction soundtracks. Das Mörtal has released material including the double single “Parasite & Ghost” (2026), the “Bury the Sorrow” and “Hotline Miami II” EPs, and the “Miami Beach Witches” album, among other releases on Bandcamp. The project has performed close to 100 shows since 2015, including more than 70 dates across the United States and Europe, at festivals such as Osheaga, Transmusicales de Rennes, FME and MEG Festival, and on tour with Vitalic, Perturbator and Carpenter Brut. “DRAIN ME” is Das Mörtal’s second single of 2026 on Lisbon Lux Records, after “Parasite & Ghost” in June.
items._cn_summary: 本文为新闻通稿性质的单曲发行通告，介绍蒙特利尔制作人Das Mörtal在Lisbon Lux Records旗下发行的双曲单曲《DRAIN ME》，收录原曲与Dan Terminus的混音版本。单曲探讨在医疗系统中反复接受检测带来的身心消耗感，原曲以电影化的铺陈开场，随后转入以琶音合成器为骨架的快节奏techno段落，融入水洗化人声处理与半速拆解。Dan Terminus的混音版本则以切片化人声、强劲打击节奏与偶尔出现的小提琴线条重塑原曲，合成低频与原声元素并置。整体制作契合暗潮与工业电子的交汇地带，但本文仅为信息发布，缺乏原创乐评的深度分析与批判视角，信息量集中于厂牌、发行日期与制作背景等基础事实。

items.body: Norwegian gothic industrial metal act Gothminister release the album “We Are All Demons” on 16 October 2026 via Elevator Records, distributed through The Orchard. The 11-track record is the project’s ninth studio album. Frontman Bjørn Alexander Brem recorded, produced, mixed and mastered “We Are All Demons” entirely himself, the first time he has handled the full process alone. Musically, the album combines gothic industrial metal with EDM elements, synthesizers, industrial guitars, theatrical vocals, female duets and choral passages. Lyrically, it addresses inner darkness and the parts of the self normally kept beneath the surface. Tracklist: Darkest Side of Earth We Are All Demons Nightmare King The Dark The Spell Welcome to Hell Salsa My Revenge Darkness Is My Throne Fearless There’s a Crown for All “We Are All Demons” follows the single “My Revenge,” released from the album on 31 July 2026. The album is available for pre-order via The Orchard’s smart link. A digipak CD edition is also listed through Napalm Records’ webshop. Gothminister has confirmed the following live dates around the release: Tour dates for Gothminister’s ‘We Are All Demons’ release 16 October 2026: Fiskepiren, Stavanger, Norway 19 November 2026: Parkteatret, Oslo, Norway 20-21 November 2026: Hellsinki Industrial Festival, Helsinki, Finland More dates are expected to be announced. About Gothminister Gothminister was formed in Oslo, Norway, in 1999 by Bjørn Alexander Brem, who handles lead vocals, programming and instruments. Guitarist Glenn Nilsen is the project’s other current member. The band’s studio discography includes “Gothic Electronic Anthems” (2003), “Empire of Dark Salvation” (2005), “Happiness in Darkness” (2008), “Anima Inferna” (2011), “Utopia” (2013), “The Other Side” (2017), “Pandemonium” (2022) and “Pandemonium II: The Battle of the Underworlds” (2024). Gothminister was also a candidate in Norway’s 2024 Eurovision Song Contest selection, Melodi Grand Prix. “We Are All Demons” follows “Pandemonium II: The Battle of the Underworlds” from 2024 and arrives 16 October 2026 via Elevator Records.
items._cn_summary: Gothminister 即将发行第九张录音室专辑《We Are All Demons》，由主唱 Bjørn Alexander Brem 独自完成全部录音、制作、混音与母带处理，这是他首次独立掌控完整制作流程。专辑将哥特工业金属与电子舞曲元素相融合，加入合成器、工业吉他音色、戏剧化人声、女声对唱与合唱段落。歌词主题围绕内在黑暗与被压抑的自我层面展开，曲目如《Darkest Side of Earth》《Nightmare King》《Welcome to Hell》等延续了乐队一贯的阴郁意象。发行厂牌为 Elevator Records，经 The Orchard 分销。乐队还确认了斯堪的纳维亚地区多场巡演，包括赫尔辛基工业音乐节。Gothminister 曾参与挪威 2024 年欧歌赛选拔 Melodi Grand Prix，积累了一定的曝光度。整体而言，这张专辑在哥特工业框架内融入电子元素，属于用户偏好的暗潮与工业范畴内较为常规的制作。

items.body: Polish solo artist Dawid Walkusz released the single “Syrena” on 25 September 2026, featuring vocalist Julia Frycz, with an official video. “Syrena” is the first single from Walkusz’s forthcoming second album, “Fantometyka,” set for spring 2027 and following his 2025 debut “Monochrom.” The song’s lyrics are in Polish. Frycz, a visual artist and vocalist who also performs with the band Emrere, sings on the track. Syrena by Dawid Walkusz, Julia Frycz Video for ‘Syrena’ Maciej Cimaszkiewicz filmed “Syrena” at seaside locations; Walkusz edited and completed post-production himself. About Dawid Walkusz Dawid Walkusz is an independent Polish vocalist, songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist. His music centres on post-punk and dream pop, with hypnagogic pop and synthwave textures. He released his debut album, “Monochrom,” on 4 April 2025, writing, producing and handling the visual side of the record entirely on his own. The eight-track album, centred on routine, overwork and stagnation, comprises “Wszystko jest szare,” “Nawiedzony dom,” “Slasher,” “24/7,” “Za wszystko,” “Zimno,” “Sen” and “Apogeum.” Walkusz’s second album, “Fantometyka,” is due in spring 2027. “Syrena,” released 25 September 2026 and featuring Julia Frycz, is its first single.

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment
(Review)

Genuine Negro Jig
(Review)

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1819年曼彻斯特彼得卢屠杀事件为主题，Sean Cooney创作原创歌曲并邀请Eliza Carthy、Sam Carter、Jennifer Reid等英国民谣音乐人参与录制，以书籍形式附带历史信件、漫画与插图，构成多媒介历史叙事项目。音乐部分采用英格兰北部工业民谣传统，通过人声、提琴与吉他讲述底层个体如Sam Bamford、Mary Fildes的故事，同时刻画士兵的蛮横与集会从期盼到惨剧的情绪转折。评论肯定了三位歌手的合作张力与音乐的情感感染力，但也指出历史细节主要落在文字中，音乐本身更多服务于叙事而非形式创新。与实验、前卫或电子等口味交集有限，但其历史介入意识与多媒介呈现方式具有一定跨界意味，适合对英国社会民谣与历史题材感兴趣的听众。
